symptom: The benchmark results panel's 'NATIVE SPEED SAMPLE' runtime number always shows the same value (Arad -> Bucharest) no matter which start/goal pair the user selects on the map.
rootcause: components/benchmark/BenchmarkCharts.tsx reads runtime exclusively from public/data/benchmark-results.json's single hardcoded sample_route object, which was seeded from one manually-run wasm/src/bin/cli.rs session for Arad->Bucharest. No per-pair native runtime data has ever been generated or shipped -- public/data/all-pairs-search.json (added separately, wasm/src/bin/export_all_pairs.rs) covers all 400 pairs but only carries structural counts (expanded/generated/peak_frontier/peak_records/peak_payload_bytes), not timing, because export_all_pairs.rs never measures elapsed time. The live WASM search path (lib/wasm/client.ts, stores/useSearchStore.ts) is structurally incapable of supplying runtime either, since SearchResult (wasm/src/metrics.rs) has no timing field, and CLAUDE.md invariant I5 forbids measuring it in the browser anyway (Chrome coarsens performance.now() to ~100us against a ~1us search).
fix: Add a dedicated PairRuntime export at the CLI/export layer (new wasm/src/bin/export_all_runtimes.rs), reusing cli.rs's Instant-based timing mechanism -- a warmup call plus repeated individually-timed runs, median taken across samples -- without touching search() or SearchResult. Generate public/data/all-pairs-runtime.json (400 pairs, row-major, index = start*20+goal) as a separate lightweight file, not folded into the 11.9MB all-pairs-search.json. Rewire BenchmarkCharts.tsx's runtime block to look up the selected route's entry from that file via the store's startCity/destinationCity instead of the static sample_route object.
automation_gap: Full byte-for-byte freshness (like verify_all_pairs.mjs does for structural data) is not meaningful here because timing is inherently non-deterministic across runs and hardware. scripts/verify_all_runtimes.mjs instead asserts coverage and structure -- all 400 pairs present, row-major, positive finite ucs/astar runtimes -- which cannot catch a stale-but-structurally-valid committed file. Accepted: runtime numbers only need to be plausible per-pair, not frozen to an exact value.
notes: This is a partial-wiring bug, not a data-shape bug: the same component (BenchmarkCharts.tsx) already correctly reads live per-route data from the store for every other metric (expanded/generated/peak queue/peak records/cost). Only the runtime block was left pointing at a placeholder static sample, because no per-pair native timing data existed yet to point it at instead.
